deploy-bot: Canary rollout v3.4.1 -> us-west-2 finished initial healthchecks, starting traffic split 10%
PD Bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-32451 created, policy=canary-rollout-failed, severity=page
PD Bot: PagerDuty: page fired to rotation 'oncall-infra'
Liam (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Seeing alert in console.
Maya S.: tagging in — what's the symptom?
Liam (oncall): 5xx spike on /v1/generate from canary hosts, error rate ~8% over 2m, latency P95 up from 120ms -> 1.3s.
Sanjay R.: logs show OOMs on transformer-worker-2 and repeated grpc CANCELled from kv-cache client. Past deploy included kernel bump + updated attention kernel.
Emily (eng): confirmed stacktraces point to attention kernel assert in quantized path. attaching snippet:
```
E 12:04:22 worker.c:452 assert(kv_len <= MAX_KV) failed
backtrace: ...
```
Liam (oncall): PD Bot: acknowledging oncall; routing to eng oncall.
PD Bot: PagerDuty: acknowledged by Liam (oncall) — escalation suspended.
Maya S.: Can we rollback canary traffic to 0% and stop rollout?
Liam (oncall): I'm going to flip traffic back to baseline. Doing via deploy console now.
deploy-bot: Traffic split update: canary=0%, baseline=100% (initiated by Liam (oncall))
deploy-bot: Canary instances draining requests, new requests routed to baseline.
Customer Success Bot: Notifying CS channel: possible customer errors on /v1/generate during 12:02-12:08 UTC, we may need proactive emails.
Sanjay R.: Good call. Root cause looks like quantized kernel regression under longer sequences (seq>1024). Canary config had longer max_seq.
Emily (eng): Is there a mitigatory patch we can apply without full rollback? e.g., restrict max_seq per request or fallback to non-quantized kernel?
Maya S.: If fallback is safe and quick we should try it, otherwise rollback is fine. Prioritize customer-facing impact.
Liam (oncall): PD Bot: adding note: traffic restored to baseline at 12:06 UTC, error rate dropping to normal in us-west-2.
PD Bot: PagerDuty: incident updated (INC-32451): mitigation=traffic-rollback, status=investigating
deploy-bot: Starting canary cleanup, terminating 4 canary instances.
Sanjay R.: I can push a quick config to force non-quant kernel on canary binary in staging build. But prod patch might require restart.
Maya S.: Can we hotfix by setting routing policy to pin long-sequence requests to baseline model only? maybe via router rule.
Emily (eng): Yes, I can apply a routing rule: if seq_len > 1024 route to baseline. Rolling it in now.
deploy-bot: Routing rule applied: seq_len>1024 -> baseline (by Emily (eng))
Liam (oncall): Observability: error rate back to ~0.7% and latency P95 gradually returning to ~130ms. Good.
PD Bot: PagerDuty: adding escalation note: no page escalation required, continue monitoring.
Maya S.: Customer impact assessment: preliminary - ~1.1k requests failed across a dozen customers (mostly long-context generation), rate-limited window ~6 minutes. Recommend outreach to top-five impacted.
Customer Success Bot: Opening CS ticket with list of affected customers and sample errors.
Sanjay R.: Next steps: revert attention kernel change in next patch, add unit test for seq_len boundary in quant path, and include a canary test with long-context synthetic load.
Maya S.: Assigning action items: @Sanjay will revert kernel change PR and add tests; @Emily will follow-up on router rule persistence; @Liam will run post-incident sanity and update incident log.
Liam (oncall): Handoff: I'm on for another 30m then handing to Ops Rotation. If no further regressions, I'll resolve PD incident.
Ops Rotation: Acknowledged handoff. Will monitor for 1h and confirm.
PD Bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-32451 acknowledged by Liam (oncall), assigned to eng-team, status=monitoring
Maya S.: Thanks team. Please add timeline to incident doc and link to postmortem when ready.
Liam (oncall): Adding timeline now. Closing thread for quick triage; will reopen if symptoms reappear. :white_check_mark:
__note: This file represents a single Slack thread. Messages are in chronological order and prefixed by sender name.
